consolidation_summary.reason: Esophageal diverticula, peptic stricture, and webs/rings are all intrinsic mechanical/structural causes of esophageal dysphagia, named together under MCC objective 26's structural-dysphagia causal category, with overlapping management (endoscopic dilation).
Peptic ulcer disease, H. pylori-induced, NSAID-induced, and stress-induced ulceration are etiology-specific subtypes of one disease entity with one shared MCC evidence base (objectives 6-1, 3-2, 14).
Traveller's diarrhea is an infectious subtype of acute diarrhea sharing objective 22-1's evidence and management approach.
Mallory-Weiss tear is explicitly named as a traumatic cause within objective 6-1's own upper-GI-bleeding causal-conditions list, not a separately evidenced diagnosis.
Diverticular bleeding is the most common cause of lower GI bleeding and is explicitly named within objective 6-2's own causal-conditions list.
Colorectal carcinoma and polyps represent one adenoma-carcinoma neoplasia continuum sharing objective 6-2's and 74's screening-based evidence.

TN presents a general viral hepatitis overview followed by four virus-specific subsections; MCC has no per-virus objective, only a general 'infection' etiology category under jaundice/abnormal-LFT objectives, so no independent per-virus MCC evidence exists to justify separate units.
